top_choice_rationale: Mircea Cărtărescu (P001) is my first choice on the common criteria. The case rests on a voice recognisable at the level of the sentence. It also rests on formal control of very large structures, in which memory, the body and dream become one imaginative construction in Blinding (the Orbitor trilogy) and Solenoid, and on the movement from poetry into large-scale prose. The citation should name the prose architecture, with poetry only as its root, and should not claim sustained development across every volume. My reading that Solenoid changes the method and does not merely restate the trilogy comes from public description and translation, not from textual demonstration or independent verification. Open uncertainties remain: how much of the effect belongs to the Romanian original and how much to translators, how well I know the poetry and early prose, and whether scale is being admired over finished execution. Adonis (P002) is a very serious second choice. Remaking the poetic language of a whole tradition over decades is a weighty achievement, and its lower place reflects the limits of what I can verify through translation, not a finding that the achievement is smaller. A poetry-only citation would be the right scope for it. No award (P000) is last: both leading proposals can be given a citation that claims only what the record supports, and the unresolved questions concern wording, not whether a distinctive writer exists.
